title: Extra Example A
summary: Find a shorter side YZ from the hypotenuse XZ and the side XY.
alt: Extra Example A: In ΔXYZ, ∠Y = 90°, XZ = 37 cm and XY = 12 cm. Calculate the length of YZ.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: We are told **∠Y = 90°**, **XZ = 37 cm** and **XY = 12 cm**. We have to find **YZ**.

steps.title: Spot the right angle
steps.narration: In ΔXYZ, **∠Y = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **XZ**. The other two sides meet at the right angle.

steps.title: Pythagoras' theorem
steps.narration: **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{XZ^2} &= \role{legA}{XY^2} + \role{legB}{YZ^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Make the unknown the subject
steps.narration: We want a **shorter side**, so subtract the known square from the hypotenuse square.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{XZ^2} &= \role{legA}{XY^2} + \role{legB}{YZ^2} \\ \role{legB}{YZ^2} &= \role{hyp}{XZ^2} - \role{legA}{XY^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute the lengths
steps.narration: Replace each side by its length.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{XZ^2} &= \role{legA}{XY^2} + \role{legB}{YZ^2} \\ \role{legB}{YZ^2} &= \role{hyp}{XZ^2} - \role{legA}{XY^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{37^2} - \role{legA}{12^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: Take the square root of both sides (a length is positive).\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{XZ^2} &= \role{legA}{XY^2} + \role{legB}{YZ^2} \\ \role{legB}{YZ^2} &= \role{hyp}{XZ^2} - \role{legA}{XY^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{37^2} - \role{legA}{12^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{1369} - \role{legA}{144} \\ &= \role{legB}{1225} \\ \role{legB}{YZ} &= \sqrt{1225} = \role{ans}{35\ \text{cm}}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse **41 cm** and one shorter side **9 cm**. Find the other shorter side.

takeaways: Find the **right angle** first — the side opposite it is the **hypotenuse**.
To find a shorter side: **subtract** the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the **square root**.
A shorter side must be **smaller** than the hypotenuse — a quick check on your answer.

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always begin with a line such as "In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," — it shows which triangle and which right angle you are using.
